questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I spoke the language of the host country/university in order to experience the culture better

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not the greatest city but very fun and interesting  to try

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not that easy. It was a bit difficult and nobody really took time showing you around.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: In denmark we use something called students guides (tutor) who show you the most basic stuff like IT and buildings and how to use facilities. The experience could have benefitted from that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorm rooms

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a communal kitchen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That it is crazy expansive especially because you don't get support through Erasmus+ (obviously)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You registrer in order to collect your student ID which is very essential to your studies. So it was all done in one swoop, but the whole application process was rather stressfull and not that easy to figure out. KU did not give sufficient guidance.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A guidance teacher, but the ratio of student per teacher was bad.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull. It took a while but the host university helped a lot

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It takes a lot of time, effort and money. But once you arrive it's really fun!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was much better than I was used to

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took mostly year 2 courses and they were great. A bit easy, but you did feel that you really learned something and that you did good within you field.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It differed a lot. We had a lot of lectures, which was a bit boring but they were short which kept it interesting. I loved the seminars as the teacher student ratio made you feel included and safe to discuss the topic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester
